claims.claim: H.R. 2965 would require the SBA's annual small-business regulatory budget to be zero or below beginning in FY2026.
The bill defines that budget as small-business costs from new, modified, or repealed federal rules.
The SBA Office of Advocacy would report annually on federal-agency rules affecting small businesses.
CBO estimated implementation would cost less than $500,000 over 2025-2030 and have no direct-spending or revenue effect.
claims.uncertainty: Estimate concerns federal implementation cost, not compliance savings or realized rulemaking effects.

claims.claim: The House passed H.R. 2965 and the Senate referred it to committee; it had not become law as of retrieval.
H.R. 2966 would add date-of-birth and citizenship, nationality, or lawful-permanent-residency certifications to SBA 7(a) and 504 loan applications.
The bill would apply the certification to an individual applicant or every beneficial owner of an applicant business.
The bill lists asylees, refugees, certain visa holders and nonimmigrants, DACA recipients, and people without lawful status as ineligible.
The House passed H.R. 2966 217-190 and it was referred to the Senate; it had not become law as of retrieval.
The initial House bill would continue FY2025 appropriations and authorities for agencies covered by all 12 annual appropriations acts through November 21, 2025.
claims.locator: CBO summary for House Rules text dated 2025-09-16
claims.uncertainty: Applies only to the initial House version.

claims.claim: The House passed the initial version 217-212 on September 19, 2025; that version was not the final law.

The Senate amendment changed the package to fund most agencies temporarily through January 30, 2026 and provide full-year FY2026 funding for Agriculture, Legislative Branch, and Military Construction-VA programs.
claims.locator: CRS summary; Public Law summary; Senate Amendment 3937 estimate
claims.uncertainty: The three full-year divisions contain many provisions; public copy names only their top-level scope.

claims.claim: Enactment ended the appropriations lapse that ran from October 1 through November 11, 2025.
The final law covered federal-employee backpay and temporarily barred specified reductions in force through the temporary-funding period, subject to exceptions.
claims.locator: Division A sections 116 and 120; CRS Federal Workforce Provisions
claims.uncertainty: The public copy should not imply an absolute bar beyond statutory definitions and exceptions.

claims.claim: The House accepted the Senate amendment 222-209 on November 12, 2025, and H.R. 5371 became Public Law 119-37 that day.
The House-stage H.R. 3944 funded FY2026 military construction, military family housing, VA benefits and health programs, and related agencies.
claims.uncertainty: The passed House text included floor amendments; the statement deliberately stays at top-level program scope.

claims.claim: The House passed its version 218-206 on June 25, 2025; it was an intermediate House action, not enactment.
The Senate later passed an expanded version, the House requested a conference, and H.R. 3944 itself did not become law; related full-year areas were later enacted through H.R. 5371.
claims.locator: H.R. 3944 conference actions; CRS legislative history; H.R. 5371 enactment
claims.uncertainty: Do not imply the enacted H.R. 5371 text was identical to the House-passed H.R. 3944 text.

claims.claim: The DeLauro motion would have instructed House conferees to accept the Senate's $8.2 billion WIC funding level.
claims.locator: Congressional Record page H4228, Clerk-read motion
claims.uncertainty: A motion to instruct is nonbinding negotiating direction and does not itself appropriate money.

claims.claim: Foushee voted Yea; the instruction failed 211-213.
Roll 180 covered Carter amendments en bloc No. 2, combining amendment numbers 1, 14, 15, 19, 25, 28, and 32.
Because the roll bundled seven distinct changes, a single plain-language policy position for Yea or Nay would conceal material differences among components.
claims.uncertainty: A complete component-by-component interpretation could be produced later, but is outside this gold slice.

claims.claim: H.Con.Res. 14 set congressional budget levels for FY2025-FY2034 and directed committees to develop later deficit, tax, spending, and debt-limit legislation.
The concurrent budget resolution did not itself amend tax rates, benefits, agency funding, or the statutory debt limit.
claims.locator: Measure form and operative budget/reconciliation instructions
claims.uncertainty: This is a legal/procedural boundary derived from the concurrent-resolution text; later legislation could and did change law separately.

claims.claim: The House adopted its initial framework 217-215 on February 25, 2025.
After Senate changes, the House accepted the revised framework 216-214 on April 10, 2025.

The final framework tied the House Ways and Means Committee's $4.5 trillion maximum deficit increase to whether specified committees achieved at least $2 trillion in net deficit reduction over FY2025-FY2034.
claims.uncertainty: These were reconciliation parameters, not an estimate that the resolution itself changed the deficit by those amounts.

claims.claim: Separate reconciliation legislation, H.R. 1, later became Public Law 119-21 on July 4, 2025.
claims.uncertainty: Must be labeled later history, not the direct effect of rolls 50 or 100.
